units.R-pos-column-A: A window cut from the record resolves fully under the record's taxid column: every k-mer supported, one run [0, L-k+1), graph_runs the same.
units.R-pos-column-B: The same property on a second record per length.
units.R-pos-header-A: A window cut from the record resolves fully under the record's header label (accession.version): every k-mer supported, one run [0, L-k+1), graph_runs the same.
units.R-pos-header-B: The same property on a second record per length.
units.R-multi: Three labels at once: the record's taxid and header support every k-mer; the unrelated kingdom's column does not support all of them (label_not_full).
units.R-junction: Two records' 100 bp windows concatenated: each column's run ends or starts where the records dictate (A's run reaches past 70 only as far as B's bases repeat A's continuation, and vice versa).
units.R-discover: Discovery (no labels) lists the source record's label, column or header, within max_labels, or states a truncation that can hide it only in a tie at full support.
units.R-trace: support: trace on 200 bp of the record under its own header answers one contiguous run over every k-mer.
units.R-budget: A 10 kb resolve under a small time budget stops with a stated prefix the record's label fully supports (or answers 503 deadline); the full 20 s resolve and the continuation from base 5000 agree with it on the prefix (relations prefix_equals).
units.R-edge-refused: Malformed or out-of-bound /resolve requests are refused with HTTP 400 and the exact text (or prefix) the host documents, before any work.
units.R-edge-accepted: Edge inputs the host accepts answer correctly: exactly k bases; an N or IUPAC code (its k-mers absent from the graph); lower case; 1,001 labels; a random sequence (absent); a budget above the cap lowered and stated; and the split cases the service refuses but the host answers.
units.R-rc: The reverse complement of a window unique on both strands: the record's header supports none of its k-mers on this basic (non-canonical) graph.
units.R-order: The same labels in another order are each answered as if alone.
units.R-twin-case: The lower-case resolve (R-edge-0007) answers byte for byte as its upper-case twin (relation same_answer).
